metric: planBefore/planAfter pairs from Calcite's current rule tests, translated to SQL, proved equivalent; 1 genuine Calcite non-equivalence refuted with a DuckDB counterexample and not counted in the 501, 55 unknown. 118 of the 167 scored pairs new to every other corpus are proved.
caveats: Calcite commit 2d28ce3 (2026-09-30). 502 of 1016 tests translate exactly; 182 leave the plan unchanged (not rewrites) and 332 are skipped with reasons (tests/fixtures/calcite_mined/skipped.jsonl). 334 of the 502 overlap SQLSolver, QED or R-Bot, whose pairs rules were developed against (tuned on test); the 168 new pairs were not used for development. While building the ANY/ALL rules, 7 held-out pairs were read (testJoinConditionOrExpansionRuleAnti, testNullSelect2, testSomeWithGreaterThanNoRowSubQuery, testSomeWithLessThanOrEqualNoRowSubQuery, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForFilterSome, testTopDownGeneralDecorrelateForSubqueryWithJoin, testNotInNullableKey); 2 of them are proved, so 61 of the 63 held-out proofs are clean. The set-operation identity rules (setop_rules.py) add 5 held-out proofs (testEmptyMinus3, testIntersectToFilterRuleNWayWithMultiSources, testIntersectToSemiJoinAll, testUnionToValuesByInList, testUnionToValuesByInList2); all 5 were in the set-operation case list those rules were developed against, so none of them is clean. The aggregate facts (smt_equivalence.py, set_aggregates.py) were developed with one held-out pair in view, testAggregateFilterToCase, which now proves, so it is not clean either. While building the ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET rules (limit_rules.py), 7 more held-out pairs were read (testLimitMerge4, testLimitMerge5, testSortRemoveDuplicateKeys, testSortRemoveDuplicateKeysWithLimit, testSortRemoveWhenAggregateMaxRowCntIsOne, testSortRemoveWhenIsOrderAndLimit, testSortUnionTransposePushesLiteralOffset); all 7 are proved, so none of them is clean. The structural aggregate rules were developed on the failing-tests triage's aggregate cases from this suite (tuned on test). The correlated LATERAL IN rules (quantified_rules.py, #384) were developed against the correlated IN pairs of the failing-tests triage; one held-out pair, testExpandProjectInWithTwoCorrelatedSubQueries, was in that list and now proves, so it is not clean. Measured on master fa78ff9 (the pairs that must stay unproven set aside), after the correlated LATERAL IN rules (#384). The DISTINCT and regrouping rules (#379) proved 2 held-out pairs (testAggregateToSemiJoinRule, testPushAggregateThroughSemiJoin) that were in that work's failing-case list before the held-out rule was announced, so they are not clean; no rule was written from them. Against master at the time they also lost 3 (testIntersectToExistsRuleMultiIntersect, testUnionToValuesByInList, testUnionToValuesByInList2), which were not investigated. The refuted pair stays in the suite as a guard (it must never be proved) and is not in the denominator. A branch whose WHERE is the constant FALSE is dropped even when its source is an opaque cut (`ORDER BY .. LIMIT 0`), which proves testSortUnionTranspose3 (smt_equivalence.py `_prune`); this is a general rule, not tuned on a case list. The pair is not among the held-out ones. Measured on master 45533e5, after batch 1 of the prover rules (#407): 439 to 446. Batch 1 proves 8 pairs it was written against, all among the 334 shared with other corpora (tuned on test), none of them held out: testExpandJoinExists, testIntersectToDistinct, testIntersectToDistinctAll, testJoinProjectTranspose1, testPushAggregateThroughOuterJoin6, testPushFilterPastProject, testReduceCastAndConsts and testSemiJoinReduceConstants. testReduceCastAndConsts and testSemiJoinReduceConstants lean on the type helper cast_rules.expression_type, which knows integer columns only. One pair proved before is now unknown: testTransitiveInferenceJoin3wayAgg (a shared pair), lost to the soundness fix that keeps a DISTINCT derived table's columns nullable until a join pins them (de432f9, #418), not to batch 1.
correctness: 0 false proofs; every proof and refutation re-run on 60 random DuckDB databases, half skewed towards the literals
coverage_of: All 834 mined Calcite tests that change the plan: the 502 scored pairs (proven, refuted, unknown) plus the 332 skipped before translation (unsupported).
held_out: 118/167 on the scored pairs new to every other corpus (168 before one was set aside as refuted), tuned on test: they scored 53/168 before any rule was developed against them; the set-operation rules were written with their unknowns in view, and 7 were read while building the ANY/ALL rules (quantified_rules.py). Rules since then were developed on the other 334 pairs and QED only; they lifted the new pairs from 76 to 78. The cast and constant rules (cast_rules.py) were developed with two held-out pairs in view, testProjectAggregateMergeSum01 and testUnionToValuesByUnionAll3; both now prove, and they lifted the new pairs from 78 to 80. The set-operation identities (setop_rules.py) then added 5 (80 to 85), all in the case list they were developed against. The aggregate facts (smt_equivalence.py, set_aggregates.py) then added 6 (85 to 91); one of them, testAggregateFilterToCase, was read while building them. The ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET rules (limit_rules.py) were developed with 7 held-out pairs in view (all proved) and added 3 new-pair proofs when they were merged. The outer-join flattening rules (outer_join_flatten.py) were written with the failing pairs of the 2026-10-02 triage in view, which included new pairs, and took the new pairs to 104 (measured on master 9ba22c8; every new pair they gained earlier was among those read). The structural aggregate rules (aggregate_rules.py) were developed with 16 new pairs from the failing-tests triage in view. The correlated LATERAL IN rules (quantified_rules.py, #384) added 1 (113 to 114), testExpandProjectInWithTwoCorrelatedSubQueries, which was in the case list they were developed against. The DISTINCT and regrouping rules (distinct_rules.py, #379) gained 2 new pairs and lost 3 against master at the time. Batch 1 (#407) left the new pairs at 118: its rules were written against shared pairs only and gained or lost no new pair.
